query: orders is taking ten times the traffic it was and nobody has changed anything upstream, where is it coming from
discriminator: Amplification: downstream load rises tenfold while inbound traffic to the caller is unchanged, and nothing fails anywhere — so the extra requests are being generated inside the system rather than arriving from outside it.

evidence.summary: request rate in the last 30 minutes: users 52.8/s inbound and unchanged from yesterday; orders 532.9/s against its usual 50/s — 10.1x, and the increase is entirely on GET /orders
a single GET /users/{id}/orders trace contains 10 client spans to orders, 10 GET /orders server spans and 10 database spans — ten identical downstream calls for one inbound request
users/OrdersClient.cs loops attempts times calling orders and assigns the result each time, with no break when the response succeeds; attempts comes from configuration and is 10
recent errors: 0 across users and orders — every one of the amplified calls returns 200

response time in the last 30 minutes (ms): users p50 rose from 20 to 93 while orders per-request latency is unchanged — the caller is slower because it is making ten round trips, not because the callee got slow
runbook retries: retry counts and backoff are configured per client; a retry that does not stop on success multiplies downstream load by the attempt count
